Notes

  1. The first two lines are the same as in Ādi 7.1; their translation is as there.
  2. Anubhāṣya: hīnārthādhika-sādhaka — He who generously fulfils the aims of the deprived, that is, of those poor in love for Kṛṣṇa; mādhuryaiśvarya-śīkara — a drop of the majesty contained in sweetness, or a drop of sweetness and majesty.
  3. The same verse as Ādi 4.2; translation as there.
  4. Anubhāṣya: in Paravyoma the container and the contained, the abode and the Lord’s form, are one.
  5. Anubhāṣya: that is, in countless yojanas. Vaikuṇṭha has no measure, as the universes of māyā have: where there is no limitation (kuṇṭha-dharma), there is “Vaikuṇṭha”.
  6. Anubhāṣya: no one knows — which is to say, the glory of Your yogamāyā is inconceivable. Brahmā praises Kṛṣṇa so after Kṛṣṇa has crushed his pride over the stealing of the calves.
  7. Anubhāṣya: the first line of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 10.12.3.
  8. Anubhāṣya: try-adhīśa — the Lord of the three: of the abodes Goloka, Paravyoma and Devī-dhāma; or of Gokula, Mathurā and Dvārakā; or of Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva, and so on; svārājya-lakṣmī — the wealth of His own nature, spirit and bliss. The explanation is in the Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta, Pūrva-khaṇḍa, 302–323.
  9. The same verse as Ādi 2.107; translation as there.
  10. The same verse as Madhya 20.318; translation as there.
  11. The same verse as Ādi 5.71 (= Madhya 20.281); translation as there. The edition’s heading gives “Brahma-saṁhitā, 5.44”.
  12. The edition’s heading: “a verse spoken by the Gosvāmipāda”. The verse number is not printed in the edition.
  13. Anubhāṣya: pradhāna is Devī-dhāma and the supreme sky Vaikuṇṭha; śubhā — free of material activity, naiṣkarmya itself, purely spiritual.
  14. The edition gives no source above this verse; where it is repeated (verse 88), the heading reads “words of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Padma Purāṇa, cited in the Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta (Pūrva-khaṇḍa, 28)”.
  15. The reference follows the edition’s heading.
  16. The edition reads maśaka, “mosquito” (stage-A text: śaśaka, “rabbit”).
  17. The same verse as 27.
  18. Anubhāṣya: if the universe is taken as a hundred koṭis of yojanas, half of it is fifty koṭis; the Anubhāṣya cites the measure of its circumference from the Sūrya-siddhānta (12.90) and the Siddhānta-śiromaṇi.
  19. In the verse: śata-koṭi, lakṣa-koṭi, niyuta-koṭi, koṭi-koṭi — a hundred, a hundred thousand, a million and ten million koṭis (a koṭi is ten million).
  20. The same verse as 51. The edition’s heading: “words of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Padma Purāṇa, cited in the Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta (Pūrva-khaṇḍa, 28)”.
  21. Anubhāṣya: Kṛṣṇa’s svarūpa accords with His human-like pastimes, yet it has no taint of worldly qualities: it is not base, not mortal, not transient, not limited and not divided.
  22. Anubhāṣya: the chariot of the gopīs’ mind is their favourable disposition; mounting it, Kṛṣṇa accepts their service. The new Kandarpa is the transcendental Madana of Vraja.
  23. Anubhāṣya: the gopīs are like the crops of the world; as a cloud rains on the crops, Kṛṣṇa pours on them streams of the nectar of His pastimes and so gives them life. In the rainy season herons fly, and the rainbow and lightning are seen.
  24. The same verse as Ādi 4.156; translation as there.
  25. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: beauty, modesty, mercy, fame, steadfastness and skilful intelligence shine in Nārāyaṇa too, but are established in Him by Kṛṣṇa; good nature, gentleness and generosity are seen in no manifestation other than Kṛṣṇa.
  26. The same verse as Ādi 4.153; translation as there.
  27. Anubhāṣya: the twenty-four and a half syllables of the Kāma-gāyatrī are like twenty-four and a half moons on Kṛṣṇa’s body (listed at 126–128); it is Kṛṣṇa’s svarūpa, for it contains the three truths — sambandha, abhidheya and prayojana. The kāma here is not of this world: the Kāma-gāyatrī and the kāma-bīja are transcendental (Anubhāṣya to Madhya 8.137).
  28. Anubhāṣya: the piety (sukṛti) that turns one to bhakti arises only from acts born of bhakti.
  29. Anubhāṣya: His form is sweeter than all other forms, His face sweeter still than His body, and His smile the sweetest of all. The edition’s heading: “words of Bilvamaṅgala in the Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta, 92”.
  30. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: sannipāta is the disorder of all three humours of the body. Struck by three — the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa’s body, face and smile — the mind thirsts for that ocean of beauty. The physician of sannipāta will not let the patient drink a drop of water; so too this illness has no physician but Kṛṣṇa, and He gives not a drop — this is the sorrow, the ill fate.
